# Theme sources become plain CSS, and the theme build copies them

## Context

Graduated from Discussion #18182 on 2026-11-17 (`[GRADUATION_APPROVED by @neo-gpt-euclid @ body 2026-11-17T04:28:06Z]`, comment 19670420; quorum with the author's signal, comment 19670104). The operator's direction for 14.0, relayed in #21210: Sass goes, a clean cut with no migration path. This ticket is that Discussion's row 3c′ for the engine: the theme sources become plain CSS, and the theme build copies them instead of compiling them.

Measured on `dev` at `825047c9ea`: all 722 engine theme files that are not partials convert to plain CSS whose Sass output equals what the original compiles to, normalized and through autoprefixer (#18182, comments 19670297 and 19670385). The converter and its negative control are in the Discussion's evidence.

## The Problem

Sass is the last build tool a development workspace needs for the engine's own styles, and it does nothing in this tree that plain CSS cannot hold: every `color.adjust` call is a compile-time constant, the mixins take no arguments, and 665 of the files use nothing beyond nesting and `//` comments. Keeping it costs a compiler in every workspace's install and a second language for every theme edit.

## The Architectural Reality

- `resources/scss/{src,theme-*}/**` holds one file per class per theme (725 files, 11 of them partials). The stylesheet loader asks for `dist/<env>/css/<folder>/<class>.css`; `theme-map.json` lists which classes have sheets in which folders.
- `buildScripts/build/themes.mjs` compiles each non-partial file with `sass.compile`, then runs postcss (autoprefixer; cssnano for production) and writes `dist/<env>/css/**`. It collects roots from the engine, from every dependency whose `package.json` names a `neo.scss` folder, and from the workspace's `resources/scss`.
- `buildScripts/helpers/watchThemes.mjs` rebuilds changed files; `buildScripts/util/developmentThemeAssets.mjs` derives the map's class census from the non-partial source tree.
- Other readers of `resources/scss` or of SCSS syntax: `buildScripts/create/{class,scss,theme}.mjs` (scaffolders), `buildScripts/helpers/convertDesignTokens.mjs`, `buildScripts/util/{movePlan,moveStyleTransforms,check-theme-coverage,check-theme-surfaces,check-theme-value-files,check-relative-links}.mjs`, and 29 test files.
- `package.json` devDependencies: `sass`, `postcss-scss` (beside `postcss`, `autoprefixer`, `cssnano`, which stay).

## The Fix

1. **Sources.** `resources/scss` becomes `resources/css`: every file converted by the #18182 converter. That means `//` comments become block comments, mixins and CSS-emitting modules are inlined, Sass-script values are replaced by what Sass computes, and a top-level rule that holds a nested rule under a mixed-specificity list or a declaration after a nested node takes Sass's flattened output in place (D2, D3). The two control-flow files take Sass's compiled output (D4). Nesting is kept everywhere else.
2. **Build.** The theme build copies `.css` sources and post-processes them as today; the map comes from the `.css` tree; the watcher copies instead of compiling. `sass` leaves `package.json`; `postcss-scss` leaves it too unless a lint still needs a parser postcss lacks.
3. **Package contract.** The `neo.scss` field of a package's `package.json` becomes `neo.css`, pointing at its plain-CSS root. A workspace's own `resources/css` replaces `resources/scss`.
4. **Every other reader** in the list above reads `.css` and `resources/css`; scaffolders write `.css`; tests follow.
5. **The converter is part of the pull request, not of the package.** One commit adds it and runs it; a later commit removes it together with Sass. The pull request body carries its proof output. The consumers' conversions run it from the pull request's head.

## Contract Ledger

| Target surface | Source of authority | Today | 14.0 | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Theme source tree | `buildScripts/build/themes.mjs` roots | `resources/scss/{src,theme-*}/**.scss` | `resources/css/{src,theme-*}/**.css` | none (clean cut) | follow-up leaf (guides) | #18182 19670385 |
| Package theme root | `themes.mjs:37` reads `neo?.scss` | `"neo": {"scss": "<dir>"}` | `"neo": {"css": "<dir>"}` | none | follow-up leaf | `themes.mjs:30-43` |
| Built output and map | `Stylesheet#addThemeFiles`, `theme-map.json` | `dist/<env>/css/<folder>/<class>.css` | unchanged | — | — | loader unchanged (3c″ is 14.x) |
| `build-themes`, `watch-themes` | `package.json` scripts | compile SCSS | copy and post-process CSS | none | follow-up leaf | — |

`Decision Record: OPTIONAL` (#21210's STEP_BACK, point 1): the source-root contract is recorded in this ticket and in the guides of the follow-up leaf.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: on the pull request's base, every converted engine file compiles to what its original compiles to (empty normalized diff), with D2 and D3 applied and the negative control passing; the pull request body carries the run.
- [ ] AC-2: `build-themes` and `watch-themes` copy `.css` sources and post-process them; `dist/development/css` serves a generated app styled, checked in a browser.
- [ ] AC-3: `sass` is gone from `package.json` and from every build script. (The fresh-workspace clause, "`npm i` in a fresh workspace installs no Sass", moved on 2026-11-17 to neomjs/create-app#61 as its AC-4: the generated workspace pins `sass` itself, and that scaffold ships with the 14.0 range on cut day.)
- [ ] AC-4: `theme-map.json` built from the `.css` tree equals the map built from the SCSS tree at the base; adding, renaming and deleting a class or theme changes it, and a removed root leaves no entry.
- [ ] AC-5: a nested child window torn out of a running app shows the sheets of an engine class, a workspace class and a package class.
- [ ] AC-6: every reader in The Architectural Reality reads `.css`; the theme lints pass on the converted tree; the unit and component suites pass.
- [ ] AC-7: the Institution's and the private package's sheets are converted, reviewed and merged the same day as this pull request (paired merge, #21210 comment 19669790).

## Out of Scope

- Dev mode reading sources in place (3c″, 14.x through #21215's server).
- The guides (their own leaf, which follows this one).
- Generated workspaces: create-app's `createScssResources.mjs` writes `resources/scss` and goes with the generator's 14.0 release (#61's window).

## Avoided Traps

- **Moving a declaration across a nested rule by property name:** a shorthand also sets its longhands (#18182, comment 19670346). Flatten the containing rule instead.
- **Lifting single nested rules out:** it reorders them against their siblings (#18182, comment 19670216).
- **Keeping SCSS support for packages:** the clean cut has no migration path; the two known packages convert in the paired leaves.
- **Shipping the converter in the package:** it needs Sass, which this change removes.

* refactor(themes): one authority for the blocks the conversion copied (#21217)

The motion vocabulary moves from five per-theme copies into src/Global.css, declared once
for every element carrying a neo-theme-* class, workspace and package themes included;
_motion.scss had called a per-theme copy a divergence trap. No other rule declares a motion
token, so moving it from the theme roots to one zero-specificity rule changes no computed
value. Without the nested @media, the theme Globals no longer need D3's flattening and
read as their sources did.

The design-token sheets and global/MouseCursor were copied into their Global sheets and
also built on their own, though no class asks for the standalone files. They go, and the
copies in the Global sheets are the authority. convertDesignTokens.mjs goes with them: it
wrote the files that no longer exist, and its output predates the hand edits since
(#18747), which a run would have reverted.

The converter gains a working-tree mode (ref `.`), and Sass's re-indented comments align
again. The tree is the converter's output for the base plus these source edits: 715 of
715 files equal.

* refactor(themes): every reader of the theme sources reads resources/css; resources/scss goes (#21217)

Scaffolders, lints, the class-move tooling, the CI scope classifier, contributor standing,
the e2e spec reach, the webpack resource copy, the lint-staged key, 20 test files and 15
source comments follow the plain-CSS tree:
- create/scss.mjs becomes create/css.mjs and writes .css stubs; create/theme.mjs parses
  with postcss and only retargets the theme class (no Sass module paths to rebase).
- moveStyleTransforms rewrites a moved sheet's relative CSS @import URLs, the one
  module reference plain CSS has; the move specs prove it with an @import bundle.
- check-theme-value-files and check-theme-surfaces drop their Sass-only comment and
  interpolation handling; check-theme-coverage drops the `global` row, a package that no
  longer exists.
- test/playwright/util/flattenCss.mjs reads nesting the browser way for the two specs that
  compiled with Sass to get flat selectors; it agrees with Sass on 715 of 715 sheets.

The converter gains three checks, each found by a reading Sass could not make:
- a second equality arm through flattenCss, with no Sass leniency;
- Sass nested properties expand to their longhands (References.css `background: {…}`,
  which a browser drops whole);
- Sass imports, placeholders and @at-root/@content left in output fail the run.
D4 now flattens only the top-level nodes holding control flow or an `&-suffix`, in place:
dashboard/Container.css keeps 32 of its 43 nodes as authored. Proof at 825047c9ea: 722 of
722 equal in both readings; the final tree: 715 of 715.

Comments that still spoke Sass (`@use`, mixins, `_motion.scss`, "the shared SCSS") now
state the plain-CSS fact, and DockRailRevealRetarget says its four keyframe pairs are
hand-written twins now, kept by its own arm.

Nothing in the engine compiles or parses SCSS any more: the theme build copies plain CSS,
and the scaffolders, lints and move tooling parse with postcss. `npm ls sass postcss-scss`
on the lockfile is empty. The converter needed both and leaves with them; the Institution's
and the private package's conversions run it from 9955e13cc6.

Chip, tab ContainerUi and DragProxyDensity loaded the standalone design-token sheets by

17 of 17 pass locally.

* feat(portal): the examples open on a groups overview, phase 1 (#21130)

What both desktop controls share, per the ticket's Fix:

- `/examples` opens an overview: the headline counts what the selected
  build publishes, the action tests its first claim, three groups to
  start with, the banded index, and every group's card by band.
- The banded index is one component, `Portal.view.examples.GroupIndex`,
  bound to the new groups store, in three presentations: the overview,
  a group page's desktop control (phase 2), the phone's sheet.
- A group counts its home records, so the counts add up to the headline.
  A group that only borrows cards shows them in parentheses, explained
  under the index.
- Below 640 px a group page keeps a crumb whose group button opens the
  full index as a sheet: it takes focus, closes on Escape and returns
  focus to the button.
- The section is no longer a tab container. `TabContainer` becomes
  `MainContainer`, a card layout over the overview and one page per
  published group. Inactive cards stay in the DOM, so each page keeps
  its scroll position. The overview replaces the Featured list, as on
  the design board.

* fix(portal): the phone overview hides its start cards, whichever sheet loads last (#21130)

The list's own `display: grid` has the same specificity as the phone
rule that hides the start cards, so the later sheet won and the index
fell below two screens at 390x664. The e2e arm for the group cards
waits for the web font before it measures a caption.

* test(portal): the examples e2e reads a settled section (#21130)

A card switch hides one page and shows the next, a build selection
closes its menu, and a card left by the pointer closes its action line
over a transition. The arms now wait for one visible page, a closed
menu and the resting card, and the card check names the cards that
miss it. Locally 19 of 22 arms pass; three stay open on the PR.

* refactor(themes): the blocks the conversion copied keep one home each (#21217)

Maryam's review of #21225 found three groups of copies where the Sass
sources had shared rules through @use and mixins. Plain CSS shares them
through the engine's own theme loading:

- The news timeline structure moves into the sheet of
  Portal.view.content.Component, the base of the tickets, pull request
  and discussion views. The theme walk loads it ancestor-first for each
  view, in the browser and in SSR, like the palette in that class's
  theme sheets.
- The dock preview accents keep one values sheet per theme, the
  dashboard Container's: Preview declares additionalThemeFiles, as
  DropIndicators does, and the five theme Preview sheets go.
- Workstation's grid tokens and header-button rules name the viewport
  and the body-mounted column-drag proxy in flat selector lists, so each
  arm keeps its own specificity.

* test(portal): the examples e2e waits for the page a reader sees (#21130)

The three open arms read the section in the middle of a card switch. The card
layout keeps inactive cards mounted here, and it flips the hidden and the
shown card in two component updates. After a sheet link the old page still
had an update in flight, so both pages showed at once and the heading
locator matched two. The shared-catalog arm clicked the build control before
the overview was back, and the Workstation arm read the Multi-Window list
before the catalog had created its page.

expectOpenPage() waits until the named page is the only one that shows, and
openOverview() until no page shows. The catalog and Connect specs pass 22 of
22, twice in full-file runs.

* feat(portal): a group page reaches the other groups by the upright index or the switcher (#21130)

Phase 2, the desktop control that OQ3 of Discussion #20742 still has to
pick. MainContainer#groupControl sets it on every page:

- list, the default and the design seat's pick: the banded index stands
  upright beside the heading and the cards, and ends above the fold of a
  720 px viewport (at 693 px for 1280x720).
- switcher, the operator's recorded preference: the crumb shows at every
  width, its group button is a pill naming how many groups the selected
  build publishes, and a link to the next group ends the cards (GroupIndex
  presentation next; after the last group it leads to the overview).

Below 640 px both keep the crumb's sheet. No card is narrower than 410 px:
two columns of 562 px beside the index at 1440x900, three of about 450 px
with the switcher.

The page places its five items on a CSS grid instead of nesting them, so the
cards stay a direct child of the page that scrolls, the root of their
intersection observer. Its rows are max-content: with auto rows the
overflowing page left no free space, and the header, which clips, shrank to
its padding under the cards. List#onIntersect now returns for a record that
a build switch dropped (a TypeError in the App Worker during the counts arm).

The config and the control the ruling does not pick leave the pull request
with that ruling.

* feat(portal): the list is the one desktop control, and its index scrolls on its own (#21130)

OQ3 is settled on Discussion #20742: the list. The switcher, its pill,
the next-group link and `groupControl` leave, and with them the
GroupIndex `next` presentation and the switcher's CSS and specs.

The upright index already scrolled on its own, but its padding sat
outside `max-height`, so at 16 groups its box ran 32 px past a 720 px
viewport. It now sizes as `border-box`. The list arm checks the box
against the viewport and scrolls the index to its last group, instead
of requiring every group above the fold, which the target's 21 groups
cannot meet at 1280x720.
